title: Canonical test bundles access and regression orchestration
creator: Aisha Patel
description: We need a defensible, auditable mechanism for storing, versioning, and gating against canonical test bundles (the curated prompt/response pairs and sentinel corpora used by evals) whenever model or config changes are introduced. This ticket scopes the product-side orchestration: naming/versioning conventions, RBAC and signer rules for immutable snapshots, CI gating integration for config/model changes, and the rollout/rollback playbook for high-risk regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Naming and versioning scheme defined and documented (semantic bundle versions + epoch metadata)
Access policy model (stewards, readers, approvers) documented and mapped to existing RBAC groups in Console
Immutable snapshot workflow implemented in the eval pipeline (signed artifact, checksum) and testable in CI staging
A gating rule that blocks config/model rollout if eval regression score delta > threshold and an automatic fallback/rollback plan exists
Runbook for steward rotation, archive TTL, and emergency rollback written and linked in the playbook
notes: Prefer 'bundle.v{major}.{minor}-{epoch}' scheme to avoid semantic drift; epoch is a date-based snapshot id (YYYYMMDD) for traceability.
Use artifact signing (artifact-signer service) so snapshots are tamper-evident; store signer id and signature in bundle metadata.
Minimum retention window = 90 days for actively served bundles; long-term archive to cheaper storage after TTL.
Owners: PM stewards own curation policy, ENG owns CI gating integration, Design to approve annotation schema for prompts/labels.
We will support both 'readonly' bundle views for readers and 'promote' APIs for stewards to mark a bundle as canonical for a rollout.
